Tantamount

TAN-tuh-mownt -- from Anglo-French tant amunter, 'to amount to as much': something tantamount 'amounts to' the same thing. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tantamount is equivalent to something else, amounting to the same thing in effect.

To the veteran sailors, refusing to wear a life vest in that storm felt tantamount to inviting disaster.

Worked Example

The company's new policy didn't technically ban vacation days, but requiring managers to approve every single one in writing, three weeks in advance, made taking time off tantamount to applying for a loan.

Tantamount means something is equivalent to something else in effect, even if it isn't officially the same thing -- the new policy never says 'no vacations,' but its burdensome process has the same practical effect as a ban.

How Tantamount Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

synonymous

synonymous: so closely associated as to be practically the same

equivalent

equivalent: equal in value, force, or effect

Antonyms

different

different: not the same as something else

opposite

opposite: completely contrary to something else

How Strong Is It? — synonymous → tantamount → equivalent

synonymous vs. tantamount

synonymous vs. tantamount: Synonymous is often used loosely to mean 'closely linked in people's minds,' while tantamount makes a stronger, more deliberate claim that two things have the exact same practical effect.

equivalent vs. tantamount

equivalent vs. tantamount: Equivalent can describe a precise, almost mathematical sameness in value, while tantamount is usually reserved for judging that an action has the same real-world consequence as something more serious.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tant-

Root — tant-: so much, as much (Latin tantus)

Root — -amount

Root — -amount: to rise, to add up to (Anglo-French amunter, from monter 'to rise' -- the same word as modern English amount)

Put it together

Put it together: Tantamount comes from Anglo-French tant amunter, 'to amount to as much': tant- (from Latin tantus, 'so much') + amount ('to rise, add up to,' from monter). Something tantamount 'amounts to' the very same thing -- the same mount that sits inside paramount.

Use the root in a new word: paramount

Use the root in a new word: paramount: Safety was paramount to the expedition leader, even when it meant turning back before the summit.
